entries.claim: The Philippines is strongly Android: Android 85.55% and iOS 14.44% of mobile web traffic in August 2026.
entries.appliesWhen: Web-traffic share; game revenue split not measured.
entries.useFor: Google Play is the primary store; App Store work is secondary.
entries.researcherNote: One source (Statcounter); no second independent origin found (web search quota exhausted).

entries.claim: The Philippines was second in Southeast Asian game downloads in Q1 2025 with 366 million, behind Indonesia (870M).
entries.appliesWhen: Sensor Tower download estimates, both stores.

support.excerpt: The Philippines and Vietnam follow with 366 million and 329 million downloads respectively.

entries.useFor: High install volume; monetisation depth not shown.
entries.researcherNote: Single origin; the report gives no Philippine revenue rank.

entries.claim: The Philippines scores 569 in EF EPI 2025 (28th of 123, High band), the strongest English proficiency of the four SEA markets covered here.

support.excerpt: The Philippines ranked second in Asia with a score of 569, also within the high-proficiency band.

entries.useFor: English captions are acceptable; a Filipino translation is not required for a broad audience.
entries.researcherNote: Both sources are EF EPI (one origin).

entries.claim: In the en_PH Google Play locale, 18 of 21 top-grossing listings share at least half their screenshots with the US listing, so publishers mostly reuse the English set for the Philippines.
entries.appliesWhen: Comparison by image identifier; 21 of the 22 packages had a US listing.

support.excerpt: Only 3 of 21 en_PH listings differ from the en_US screenshot set by more than half.

entries.useFor: An English deck is the norm for the Philippines; no separate Filipino set is needed.
entries.researcherNote: Chart order from Similarweb (used only to pick packages). Single snapshot of one chart on one day; chart mix is dominated by MOBA, battle-royale, casual and card games, not roguelikes.

entries.claim: In the 22 top-grossing games on Philippines Google Play (26 Sep 2026 chart), the first phone screenshot set was landscape in 16 and portrait in 6; the median was 7 screenshots (range 5 to 9).
entries.appliesWhen: Top-grossing games of all genres in the Philippines.
entries.useFor: Landscape is the local top-grossing norm, driven by genre mix.
entries.researcherNote: Chart order from Similarweb (used only to pick packages). Single snapshot of one chart on one day; chart mix is dominated by MOBA, battle-royale, casual and card games, not roguelikes.

entries.claim: Habby's Capybara Go, Archero 2 and Survivor.io show the same English screenshot sets in the Philippine and US listings.

support.excerpt: en_PH image sets are identical to en_US for all three Habby titles.

entries.useFor: Competitors do not localise for the Philippines.
entries.researcherNote: Direct observation by image identifier; English captions viewed for the US set.

entries.claim: A localisation vendor says Filipinos mix Tagalog and English (Taglish) fluidly, and that urban Gen Z and older users differ in platforms (TikTok/Instagram vs Facebook and long video).
entries.appliesWhen: General localisation advice; no game data.

support.excerpt: a seamless, hybrid blend of Tagalog and English that shifts tone, pace, and nuance depending on context.

entries.useFor: English or Taglish captions are fine; no evidence for Tagalog-only art.
entries.researcherNote: An earlier note claimed provincial audiences prefer Tagalog; the fetched page does not say that.

entries.claim: A payments vendor reports digital wallets are the most popular Philippine game payment method, used by 39% of players, led by GCash, and that players are price-sensitive.
entries.appliesWhen: Filipino gamers; methodology and sample not disclosed.

support.excerpt: Digital wallets have become the most popular payment method in the Philippines, used by 39% of players.

entries.useFor: Local wallet acceptance is a minor conversion hook, not a store-image finding.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor with a commercial interest; no methodology.

entries.claim: In March 2023 the Philippine MTRCB rejected expanding its mandate to video games, so no enforced game-rating or content law was found for the Philippines.
entries.appliesWhen: Senate Bill 1063 proposed extending MTRCB to games; status after 2023 not found.

support.excerpt: Hindi po kakayanin ng MTRCB kung isasama pa po ang video games.

entries.useFor: No Philippine age label is required on store art as far as found.
entries.researcherNote: 2023 news; absence of a law is not proven.
